app.title: PetroLog
app.summary: A person uploads a well-log file and views its curves as tracks down a depth window, with curves of their choice in each track and optional depth markers. They can group depth samples into clusters on chosen curves, and set any two curves against each other in a crossplot. Next they compute derived curves from editable model parameters, then apply cutoffs to pick the depth intervals that qualify as reservoir and pay. The result is a zone table, a summary by depth bin, tracks with the zones marked and a plain-language narrative, all of which can be downloaded as CSV, LAS or text.

task.text: Compute rock and fluid properties from a well's log curves and find the depth intervals that pass reservoir and pay cutoffs, with a written summary.

data.text: Log curves from one well, each recorded at regular depth steps, plus the properties, flags and zone ids derived from them
data.item: a depth sample with a value for each log curve

stage.text: quick-look petrophysical evaluation of a logged well, from raw curves to net-pay intervals

mechanism.text: Five tabs share the uploaded log through session state. Each plots curves as tracks on a shared depth axis, either inside a depth window the person sets or shaded by cluster or pay band. Parameter forms drive the computation of new curves and the picking of cutoff zones, and the results are shown as tables, headline totals, a narrative and download buttons.
patterns: stacked tracks on a shared axis

field.text: quick-look well-log petrophysics and net-pay interpretation in petroleum geoscience

workflow.name: compute derived properties along a profile and pick the intervals that pass cutoffs

steps.here: Upload a LAS file. Curve names from different vendors are mapped to standard names, null values are removed and depth is converted to metres.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A depth-window slider and four track pickers draw the chosen curves side by side down the depth axis, with optional comma-separated depth markers. The window can be downloaded as PNG or CSV.
Choose a cluster count and feature curves, then run K-Means. Clusters are drawn as coloured bands behind the tracks, and the labelled data can be downloaded.

steps.step: compare two variables against each other
steps.here: Pick an X curve, a Y curve and an optional colour curve within a depth window to draw a crossplot. The plot and its points can be downloaded.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Choose a shale-volume model and enter matrix and fluid density, clean and shale GR, and Archie a, m, n and Rw. This computes porosity, shale volume, water saturation, hydrocarbon pore-volume index and gas, fracture and invasion flags, with optional pay shading on the tracks. The result can be downloaded as CSV or LAS.

steps.step: pick the intervals that pass cutoffs and total them
steps.here: Cutoffs for maximum VSH, minimum PHI, maximum SW and minimum thickness pick contiguous net-reservoir and net-pay zones. These are shown as headline totals, a zone table, a net-to-gross table by depth bin and tracks with pay tops and bases marked.

A narrative is generated that states the cutoffs used and grades each pay zone's porosity, shaliness, water and hydrocarbon volume in words, with notes on gas and fractures. It can be downloaded as text, and the interpreted data as CSV and LAS.

distinctive: Shale volume can come from any of four empirical models (Linear, Larionov young, Larionov old, Steiber), and water saturation follows Archie's law with exponents and water resistivity the person can edit.
A zone is a contiguous run of depth samples that passes every cutoff and meets a minimum thickness. Net reservoir (shale and porosity only) is kept apart from net pay (which adds water saturation).
Each zone counts flagged samples, such as gas from density–neutron separation and fractures or washouts from caliper spikes.
Net-to-gross and pay fraction are totalled in depth bins whose size the person sets.
Results are written back out as a standard LAS log file with the derived curves and zone ids added.
